chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who entered the mosque and the prayer had commenced. So while he was standing praying, the Mu'adhdhin gave the call to prayer and announced the establishment of the prayer. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him pray two Rak'at, then let him resume the prayer with the Imam, and let the two Rak'at be voluntary.'
ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they arrive at the mosque after the Imam has already started the congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi clarifies the procedure for a worshipper who enters the mosque after the congregational prayer has commenced, distinguishing between the obligatory Fard and the voluntary Nafl. It establishes that the initial two Rak'at serve as a synchronization mechanism, allowing the individual to join the Imam seamlessly while maintaining the integrity of both prayers. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on order and intentionality in congregational worship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who enters the Masjid and the Salāt has commenced. So while he was standing, praying, the Muezzin recited the Azan and established the Salāt. Heasws said: ‘So let him pray two Rak’at, then let him resume the Salāt with the Imam, and let the two Rak’at be (classified as) voluntary’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who enters Masjid and begins Salah (prayer). While he is standing up in Salah (prayer) Adhan is said and Salah (prayer) begins. He (the Imam) said, ‘He can perform it as a two Rak‘at, then commence Salah (prayer) with the Imam and the two Rak‘at has to be optional Salah (prayer)”’
